reviews.content: I had heard of this book from my friends, so when my sister found she was pregnant, I decided buy it for her. Well, even though I've nevr read it, she raves about it and I trust her opinion. Her comments focus on it's easy to read/understand format and it covers just about everything you could ever think of or run into. She thanks me on a regular basis for finding this book for her, and that makes me feel good.

reviews.content: I love this book. It's so easy to read and so informative. It's set up is similar to a magazine.. It's just really easy to read. A lot of the book is in a QandA format which is nice and straight forward. It covers pretty much everything. I even bought a copy for my best friend for Christmas and she loves it too! It has a lot of interesting facts and really puts you at ease. It covers everything from before you even think about getting pregnant to way past giving birth. Great read!

reviews.content: I've enjoyed reading this book so far, especially since it reads easily and covers a variety of topics. The tone of the book is very personal and feels like a friend offering advice and wisdom. The authors advocate for alternative and homeopathic medicine often throughout this book, which I found disappointing since I was looking for a more credible source of information grounded in science and research. In addition, there are significant formatting issues with this book as a NOOK Book, meaning that you'll flip a page and go from the middle of one section to the middle of another.

reviews.content:
I did not find this book to be particularly useful. t does a good job of alerting you to every possible thing you could do that "might" be harmful to your baby, but it seems like the final advice is always, "Talk to your practitioner. " could talk to my doctor without shelling out for this book, if I'm going to pay for something like this, I expect it to contain information I can use. t feels like the authors are so desperate to avoid a potential lawsuit, they won't come out and actually recommend anything.

One example is the section on acne medication- we are told not to use Accutane because it causes birth defects (fair enough. ) We are then told that salicylic acid, BHA, benzoyl peroxide, glycolic acid, and azelaic "may" or "are probably" safe to use, but to "ask your practitioner. " The book does not list one single product that you can actually use. We are then advised to prevent acne by "drinking plenty of water" and "keeping your face clean" (using what, exactly???) Yeah, because that works like a charm for most people with acne. Looking on WebMD, I quickly got a straight answer on this (benzoyl peroxide yes, everything else, no) for free.

Many of the other warnings are equally ludicrous. We are told not to worry about it too much if you have used cocaine just once or twice before you realized you were pregnant (but let's lay off the cocaine going forward!), but to avoid green tea. Really? So I'm supposed to feel guilty about the green tea with ginger that actually helps with my nausea (and which my practitioner said was totally fine when I asked her about it), but not to worry about all that cocaine I had been using? Seriously?
